title: GoF Design Patterns

source_reference.title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
source_reference.role: Canonical collection attribution and category reference; article prose, examples, and diagrams are original educational explanations.

import_source: patterns.json (individual articles and HTML reading edition are not loaded)

patterns.title: Factory Method
patterns.short_description: Let a reusable workflow delegate object creation to an overridable method.
use_when: A shared workflow needs different concrete collaborators
A framework needs an extension point for creating a product
not_ideal_when: The only need is a small conditional constructor
Runtime configuration would be clearer than subclassing
example_user_queries: My framework knows too much about the classes plugins create.
I keep copying a workflow just to change one object.
How can subclasses choose the component a process uses?
Every new exporter forces changes in the main workflow.
I want an extension point without exposing the entire algorithm.
A reusable process needs different implementations of one collaborator.
How can I share the steps but vary the object being created?
I need a library to call user supplied creation logic.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: A shared publishing workflow calls a creation hook; specialized creators supply the concrete exporter.
graphic.alt_text: A shared publishing workflow calls a creation hook; specialized creators supply the concrete exporter.

patterns.title: Abstract Factory
patterns.short_description: Create families of compatible products through one coherent creation interface.
use_when: Several collaborators must belong to the same implementation family
A client should switch a whole platform or provider without mixing variants
not_ideal_when: Only one independent product varies
Product families have no meaningful compatibility constraint
example_user_queries: My components accidentally mix implementations from different providers.
How can I switch a whole backend consistently?
Different platforms need matching sets of UI components.
Selecting each dependency separately leads to incompatible combinations.
I need one choice to configure several related collaborators.
My tests should replace a complete family of infrastructure objects.
How can client code avoid knowing which platform it runs on?
Adding a provider duplicates wiring across several constructors.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: One family choice supplies a coherent set of widgets rather than independently mixing products.
graphic.alt_text: One family choice supplies a coherent set of widgets rather than independently mixing products.

patterns.title: Builder
patterns.short_description: Separate staged construction of a complex result from the result itself.
use_when: An object needs several meaningful construction steps
Different representations share a construction process
not_ideal_when: A small immutable value can be constructed clearly with named arguments
The staged API permits invalid intermediate objects to escape
example_user_queries: My constructor has too many parameters to read safely.
Building a report requires several coordinated steps.
I want the same assembly process to produce different outputs.
Optional settings make object creation confusing.
How can I keep partially configured objects away from callers?
I need to validate a result after all its parts are supplied.
Object construction is tangled with the finished object behavior.
Several callers repeat the same complicated setup sequence.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Construction state stays in the builder; completion validates it and produces a finished report.
graphic.alt_text: Construction state stays in the builder; completion validates it and produces a finished report.

patterns.title: Prototype
patterns.short_description: Create a new object by copying an existing configured representative.
use_when: A configured template is easier to copy than reconstruct
Concrete types should supply their own duplication behavior
not_ideal_when: Object identity represents an external resource that cannot meaningfully be copied
Copying would silently preserve shared mutable state
example_user_queries: I need several independent variants of a configured object.
Recreating a template requires repeating a lot of setup.
My editor should duplicate items without knowing their concrete types.
How can plugins define how their objects are copied?
I want to start from an existing example and customize it.
Copying an object accidentally changes the original.
Objects are expensive to configure from scratch.
How should cloning handle nested mutable data?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: A domain-aware copy keeps the template configuration, gives the copy a new identity, and separates mutable annotations.
graphic.alt_text: A domain-aware copy keeps the template configuration, gives the copy a new identity, and separates mutable annotations.

patterns.title: Singleton
patterns.short_description: Restrict a class to one instance within a defined scope and expose shared access to it.
use_when: A resource genuinely requires one coordinated owner within a process
A class must enforce a single-instance lifecycle rather than merely happen to be shared
not_ideal_when: The only motivation is convenient global access
Multiple test or tenant contexts need independent instances
The actual uniqueness requirement spans processes
example_user_queries: I need one component to own a process-wide resource.
Global shared state makes my tests affect each other.
Does using one instance require a singleton class?
I want every caller to use the same coordinator.
My singleton exists once in each worker and still races.
How can I control who initializes a shared service?
A globally accessible object hides too many dependencies.
I need to distinguish one per process from one for the whole system.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: A shared instance is unique only within its defined scope. Another process can have another instance.
graphic.alt_text: A shared instance is unique only within its defined scope. Another process can have another instance.

patterns.title: Adapter
patterns.short_description: Translate an existing interface into the contract a client expects.
use_when: An existing component has useful behavior behind an incompatible interface
A boundary should isolate an external API from application code
not_ideal_when: The underlying behaviors cannot satisfy the expected contract
Both interfaces are owned locally and can be simplified directly
example_user_queries: A vendor API does not match the interface my application uses.
I want to replace a dependency without changing every caller.
Integration details keep leaking into business logic.
My existing library has the right behavior but the wrong method names.
Two systems express the same operation with different data formats.
How can I wrap a legacy component behind a cleaner contract?
I need to translate external failures into application-level results.
My callers should not depend on provider-specific response objects.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The application uses its mail contract; the adapter translates payloads and results at the provider boundary.
graphic.alt_text: The application uses its mail contract; the adapter translates payloads and results at the provider boundary.

patterns.title: Bridge
patterns.short_description: Separate an abstraction from its implementation so two dimensions can vary independently.
use_when: Two independent design dimensions are multiplying subclasses
High-level operations should work with interchangeable lower-level implementations
not_ideal_when: There is only one actual dimension of variation
Most combinations are invalid and the separation would imply false independence
example_user_queries: Adding a new platform doubles the number of classes.
I have subclasses for every combination of feature and backend.
My abstraction and implementation need to evolve separately.
How can several high-level tools share interchangeable low-level implementations?
A class hierarchy mixes product features with transport choices.
I need to choose a renderer without changing each shape class.
Two dimensions of variation keep getting tangled together.
How can I avoid a subclass for every possible pairing?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Shape variants use a renderer contract. Shape and renderer families can evolve along separate dimensions.
graphic.alt_text: Shape variants use a renderer contract. Shape and renderer families can evolve along separate dimensions.

patterns.title: Composite
patterns.short_description: Give individual objects and groups a common interface for recursive tree operations.
use_when: A domain contains nested part–whole structures
Clients should treat a leaf and a group uniformly for selected operations
not_ideal_when: The relationship is primarily a graph with shared ownership or cycles
Leaves and groups have almost no meaningful common operations
example_user_queries: My code handles one item and a group through separate branches.
I need to operate on nested groups of objects.
Folders and individual files should share some behavior.
A document contains sections inside other sections.
How can an operation apply to an entire tree without special cases everywhere?
My drawing editor groups shapes recursively.
Tree traversal logic is duplicated across callers.
I want a meaningful common interface for leaves and containers.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Groups contain components, including nested groups. A shared move operation follows the part–whole tree.
graphic.alt_text: Groups contain components, including nested groups. A shared move operation follows the part–whole tree.

patterns.title: Decorator
patterns.short_description: Compose optional responsibilities by wrapping an object behind the same contract.
use_when: Independent behaviors need to be combined at runtime
Inheritance is producing a class for every feature combination
not_ideal_when: Wrapper order cannot be understood or constrained
The feature needs broad access to internal invariants rather than the public contract
example_user_queries: Optional features keep multiplying my subclasses.
I want to add behavior to one object without changing its class.
Logging and validation should compose around the same service.
How can I combine features at runtime?
I need wrappers that callers can use through the original interface.
A feature matrix is turning into dozens of class names.
The order of my wrappers changes the result.
I want behavior layers with clear ownership and cleanup.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: This writer composition compresses before encrypting, then stores the bytes. Reversing wrappers changes the operation.
graphic.alt_text: This writer composition compresses before encrypting, then stores the bytes. Reversing wrappers changes the operation.

patterns.title: Facade
patterns.short_description: Offer a focused interface over a subsystem with several collaborating components.
use_when: Clients repeatedly coordinate the same subsystem operations
Most callers need a simpler view than the full subsystem API
not_ideal_when: The interface would conceal essential failure or consistency information
The facade is becoming a universal service for unrelated operations
example_user_queries: Every caller needs to understand several internal components.
Starting one operation requires a complicated sequence of API calls.
I want a simple entry point for a subsystem.
Internal implementation changes keep affecting application code.
How can I hide routine coordination without hiding failures?
My tests need to replace a whole subsystem boundary.
Several screens repeat the same orchestration code.
A library exposes far more detail than most clients need.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The export facade owns routine subsystem coordination; callers request one meaningful export operation.
graphic.alt_text: The export facade owns routine subsystem coordination; callers request one meaningful export operation.

patterns.title: Flyweight
patterns.short_description: Share reusable intrinsic state while keeping context-specific state outside the shared object.
use_when: A very large population repeats the same substantial state
Shared state can remain stable across many contexts
not_ideal_when: Most object state is unique or heavily mutable
Sharing overhead exceeds the measured memory benefit
example_user_queries: Millions of small objects repeat the same metadata.
My editor uses too much memory for repeated text styles.
How can I share stable data without mixing per-instance state?
Each map marker duplicates the same visual assets.
I need to separate shared properties from position and selection.
Caching whole objects accidentally shares mutable state.
Would interning repeated values reduce memory usage?
How can many logical objects use fewer physical representations?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Two logical trees retain independent location and selection while referencing one shared intrinsic tree type.
graphic.alt_text: Two logical trees retain independent location and selection while referencing one shared intrinsic tree type.

patterns.title: Proxy
patterns.short_description: Stand in for another object to mediate access while preserving its useful interface.
use_when: Access requires lazy creation or a controlled boundary
A remote or expensive subject needs a local representative
not_ideal_when: Mediation would make critical latency or failure behavior misleading
The proxy bypasses the authoritative enforcement boundary
example_user_queries: I want to load an expensive object only when it is used.
A local interface needs to represent a remote service.
How can access be mediated without changing ordinary callers?
Some operations need permission checks before delegation.
I need to cache requests behind a stable service contract.
My wrapper should control when the real object is created.
Remote calls look local and their failures surprise callers.
How can I avoid exposing a resource directly to every client?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The client asks a lazy image proxy to render. The proxy loads its real image on first demand, then delegates.
graphic.alt_text: The client asks a lazy image proxy to render. The proxy loads its real image on first demand, then delegates.

patterns.title: Chain of Responsibility
patterns.short_description: Let a request pass through candidate handlers without coupling its sender to a specific receiver.
use_when: The appropriate receiver depends on context or runtime configuration
Candidate handlers need a deliberate fallback order
not_ideal_when: The receiver is fixed and direct delegation is clearer
Several independent listeners must all receive the same event
example_user_queries: A request should fall back through several possible handlers.
The sender should not know which component handles a request.
I need a configurable order for resolving a value.
Unhandled requests disappear silently in my routing code.
My input event should reach the nearest suitable receiver.
Adding a handler means editing a central conditional.
I want to separate request creation from receiver selection.
How can I make handler ordering and stopping rules explicit?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: A shortcut moves outward only when a candidate passes. Handling stops propagation; the application is a fallback.
graphic.alt_text: A shortcut moves outward only when a candidate passes. Handling stops propagation; the application is a fallback.

patterns.title: Command
patterns.short_description: Represent an operation as an object or value so it can be stored, scheduled, or composed.
use_when: Actions need to outlive the UI event that created them
Operations need queuing, history, or explicit execution ownership
not_ideal_when: A direct function call already expresses the complete need
The design assumes every operation can be automatically undone
example_user_queries: Buttons and shortcuts duplicate the same action logic.
I want to queue operations for later execution.
How can actions be represented as data rather than immediate calls?
My editor needs an undo history.
I need to record which operations were requested.
A background worker should execute a request created elsewhere.
I want to combine several actions into one meaningful operation.
How can retry and execution ownership be explicit?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Several invokers can create the same action representation. Execution and undo history have explicit owners.
graphic.alt_text: Several invokers can create the same action representation. Execution and undo history have explicit owners.

patterns.title: Interpreter
patterns.short_description: Model a small language through expression objects that evaluate its grammar.
use_when: A compact recurring expression language needs domain-specific meaning
Grammar alternatives map cleanly to a small set of expression types
not_ideal_when: The language is large or requires sophisticated parsing and tooling
A mature parser or query language already meets the need
example_user_queries: Users need to express small rules rather than fixed options.
I want to evaluate combinations of domain-specific expressions.
Conditional logic is being encoded in ad hoc strings.
How can a small grammar become an explicit object structure?
My rule language needs predictable evaluation semantics.
I need to keep parsing separate from evaluating expressions.
A few recurring boolean expressions should be composable.
When does a custom mini-language become too complex?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Compound expressions recursively evaluate terminal expressions against a deliberate task context.
graphic.alt_text: Compound expressions recursively evaluate terminal expressions against a deliberate task context.

patterns.title: Iterator
patterns.short_description: Traverse elements through a common protocol without exposing a collection’s representation.
use_when: Clients need sequential access to different storage structures
Traversal state should be separate from the collection itself
not_ideal_when: A client needs random access that the traversal interface does not provide
Traversal hides resource ownership or unstable mutation semantics
example_user_queries: My algorithm should work on several kinds of collections.
I want to traverse a tree without exposing its internal nodes.
Loading every result at once uses too much memory.
How can two readers walk the same collection independently?
Collection storage details keep leaking into callers.
I need a lazy sequence with a clear end condition.
What should happen if data changes during traversal?
A database cursor needs predictable cleanup when iteration stops.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Independent iterators own separate positions over the same collection. The client consumes elements through the traversal protocol.
graphic.alt_text: Independent iterators own separate positions over the same collection. The client consumes elements through the traversal protocol.

patterns.title: Mediator
patterns.short_description: Place collaboration rules in a coordinator instead of spreading them across peer objects.
use_when: Many components know too much about one another
Interaction rules change independently from component behavior
not_ideal_when: A few direct relationships are already clear
The coordinator would absorb unrelated domain logic
example_user_queries: My UI controls all call one another directly.
Changing one component breaks several peers.
Where should collaboration rules between components live?
A dialog has tangled enable and disable logic.
I want to reuse a component outside its current screen.
How can I reduce peer-to-peer dependency relationships?
The same interaction rule is repeated in several objects.
My event coordinator is becoming too large to understand.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: Participants report events to one scoped mediator, which owns the collaboration rules and updates other participants.
graphic.alt_text: Participants report events to one scoped mediator, which owns the collaboration rules and updates other participants.

patterns.title: Memento
patterns.short_description: Capture restorable state without requiring the caretaker to inspect its internal representation.
use_when: An object needs snapshots or rollback of its own state
History management should remain separate from state representation
not_ideal_when: Restoration is expected to reverse external effects
Snapshots are too expensive or incompatible without a defined policy
example_user_queries: My editor needs to restore an earlier state.
The undo manager knows too much about object internals.
How can I save a checkpoint without exposing private fields?
I want rollback for a local configuration change.
Copying random fields does not restore a valid object.
Snapshots consume too much memory.
A saved state must survive changes to the object structure.
What should be included in a restoration boundary?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The originator captures and restores its coherent state. The caretaker retains an opaque memento without editing its internals.
graphic.alt_text: The originator captures and restores its coherent state. The caretaker retains an opaque memento without editing its internals.

patterns.title: Observer
patterns.short_description: Let subscribers receive notifications when a subject changes without hard-coding its dependents.
use_when: An open-ended set of dependents reacts to one subject
The subject should publish change information without knowing each consumer
not_ideal_when: A fixed direct call is clearer
Subscribers rely on unspecified order or atomic delivery
example_user_queries: Several views need to react when one model changes.
My model knows every component that depends on it.
How can new listeners be added without editing the publisher?
A subscriber remains active after its screen closes.
Notifications trigger recursive updates.
I need to distinguish a state snapshot from a change event.
Listener ordering is creating hidden dependencies.
One failing subscriber prevents others from being notified.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The document publishes one coherent title change to independent subscribers. Their subscription lifetimes remain explicit.
graphic.alt_text: The document publishes one coherent title change to independent subscribers. Their subscription lifetimes remain explicit.

patterns.title: State
patterns.short_description: Move state-dependent behavior into explicit state objects and delegate through the current state.
use_when: Several operations repeatedly branch on the same lifecycle state
States have distinct behavior and deliberate transitions
not_ideal_when: A small transition table or enum remains easier to read
The design hides transition rules across too many objects
example_user_queries: Every method has a switch on the same status field.
My workflow behaves differently depending on its lifecycle stage.
Invalid actions are scattered across conditional branches.
How can I make state transitions and allowed operations explicit?
Adding a status means editing many methods.
An object changes behavior after an event.
I need to distinguish interchangeable policies from lifecycle states.
My state classes make it difficult to see the whole transition graph.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The upload delegates behavior to its active state. Pause and resume are lifecycle transitions; completion leads to a different valid operation set.
graphic.alt_text: The upload delegates behavior to its active state. Pause and resume are lifecycle transitions; completion leads to a different valid operation set.

patterns.title: Strategy
patterns.short_description: Make a varying algorithm or policy explicit and replaceable behind a common contract.
use_when: A task has several meaningful interchangeable algorithms
Policy varies independently from the context that uses it
not_ideal_when: There is only one trivial implementation with no useful boundary
Strategies cannot honestly fulfill the same behavioral contract
example_user_queries: My method has a large conditional for different algorithms.
I want to choose a policy at runtime.
Different customers need different rules for the same task.
How can I test an algorithm separately from its surrounding workflow?
Adding a variant keeps changing the main service.
I need interchangeable behavior without a subclass for the whole service.
Several implementations should return the same kind of result.
How can a function parameter replace a strategy class?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The order workflow delegates to a pricing contract; the selected algorithm is separate from the stable surrounding workflow.
graphic.alt_text: The order workflow delegates to a pricing contract; the selected algorithm is separate from the stable surrounding workflow.

patterns.title: Template Method
patterns.short_description: Define a stable algorithm skeleton and allow subclasses to customize selected steps.
use_when: Several processes share an invariant sequence with specific variation points
An inheritance-based framework needs constrained extension hooks
not_ideal_when: Runtime composition fits the variation better than inheritance
Subclasses must frequently bypass the fixed sequence
example_user_queries: Several implementations copy the same workflow skeleton.
I want extensions to customize steps without changing their order.
A base process should enforce validation before execution.
How can I keep common cleanup in one place?
Subclasses repeat orchestration but differ in one stage.
I need narrow hooks rather than overriding the whole method.
When is composition clearer than inheriting a process?
My subclass hooks depend on undocumented internal state.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: The base importer owns step order. A format-specific override supplies reading while shared validation and cleanup stay in the workflow.
graphic.alt_text: The base importer owns step order. A format-specific override supplies reading while shared validation and cleanup stay in the workflow.

patterns.title: Visitor
patterns.short_description: Organize operations separately from a stable family of element types using type-specific dispatch.
use_when: A stable object structure needs many different operations
Type-specific operations should not all live inside the element classes
not_ideal_when: Element types change frequently while operations remain stable
Traversal or pattern matching can express the operation more simply
example_user_queries: My syntax tree classes contain too many unrelated operations.
I want to add analyses without editing every element implementation.
Different node types need different handling in one operation.
How can behavior be organized by operation rather than by data type?
I keep using type checks throughout a tree walk.
The object structure is stable but new reports keep arriving.
Adding a node type breaks many external operations.
When is a visitor preferable to pattern matching?
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with objects, interfaces, composition, and inheritance

graphic.caption: An element accepts the selected operation and dispatches to its type-specific visitor method. The visitor owns the operation.
graphic.alt_text: An element accepts the selected operation and dispatches to its type-specific visitor method. The visitor owns the operation.
